tema: Analyses clinical and laboratory parameters in post-COVID-19 syndrome with fatigue and compares them with non-COVID post-infectious ME/CFS.
diseno: Prospective observational cohort: 42 post-COVID patients (29 women/13 men, median 36.5 years) with fatigue and exercise intolerance at 6 months, versus a matched non-COVID ME/CFS cohort; handgrip strength and biomarkers; non-parametric statistics.
hallazgos: 19 patients met the 2003 Canadian Criteria; severity was similar to non-COVID ME/CFS; handgrip strength was reduced and was associated with haemoglobin, IL-8 and CRP (or with NT-proBNP, bilirubin and ferritin in the ME/CFS subgroup).
conclusion: The associations suggest low-grade inflammation and hypoperfusion as possible mechanisms.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (long COVID, handgrip strength, IL-8, CRP); the extracted conclusions are actually the statistical methods section and provide no conclusions of their own.

tema: Evaluates the efficacy of a neuroprotective therapy (succinate anion coordination complex, SACC) versus placebo in post-COVID CFS using fMRI.
diseno: Prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; 30 patients with post-COVID asthenic syndrome (15 SACC, 15 placebo); MFI-20, MoCA and FAS-10 scales and resting-state and cognitive-task fMRI (3 T) before and after treatment.
hallazgos: The SACC group reduced asthenic symptoms more (MFI-20: -20 versus -12 points; p = 0.043) and improved more on the MoCA (2 versus 1 point; p < 0.05); the fMRI data suggest improvement in functional cognitive state.
conclusion: The authors claim the superior efficacy of SACC over placebo on post-COVID fatigue and cognitive impairment, supported by neuroimaging techniques.
triangulacion: The sources agree on the figures; the PDF conclusions qualify the abstract by acknowledging a small sample, a single centre (pilot study), lack of healthy controls, a possible learning effect on the MoCA and short follow-up. The keywords focus on fMRI and cognition.

tema: Evaluates the safety and efficacy of the monoaminergic stabilizer (-)-OSU6162 in ME/CFS.
diseno: Randomized placebo-controlled trial in 62 patients; primary outcomes: Mental Fatigue Scale (MFS) and CGI-C; secondary: FibroFatigue, BDI, pain and neuropsychological tests; assessment at baseline, at 1 and 2 weeks and at 6 weeks.
hallazgos: Both groups improved on the MFS and CGI-C after treatment, with no differences between groups; the (-)-OSU6162 concentration correlated with changes in MFS, FF and BDI, and the effect was greater in patients on antidepressants.
conclusion: The drug was safe and well tolerated; it did not outperform placebo overall, but did so in the subgroup receiving concomitant antidepressant treatment.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the structured abstract itself and agree with it; the keywords reflect mental fatigue, depression and safety well.

tema: To retrospectively compare the outcome of faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) versus oral approaches in ME/CFS with IBS.
diseno: Retrospective study of 42 patients (21 on oral treatments: nutrition, probiotics, prebiotics; 21 with FMT of 10 implants via the rectal route); percentage improvement by clinical assessment; Mann-Whitney.
hallazgos: The median improvement was significantly greater in the FMT group (U = 111.5; p = 0.003).
conclusion: FMT would be safe and promising for CFS associated with IBS; adequately powered RCTs are required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the keywords emphasize probiotics and nutritional therapy more than FMT. Evaluation based only on the author's clinical judgement limits robustness, although the conclusions do not qualify this.

tema: Compares the cardiorespiratory capacity and neuromuscular function of people with CFS and fibromyalgia with healthy controls.
diseno: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42020184108); 99 studies with 9853 participants (5808 patients, 4405 controls); risk of bias with EPHPP.
hallazgos: Lower VO2max, anaerobic threshold and peak lactate, and lower neuromuscular function (MVC, fatigability, voluntary activation, muscle mass, perceived exertion) in CFS and fibromyalgia, with moderate to large effect sizes.
conclusion: People with CFS and fibromyalgia show lower cardiorespiratory capacity and muscle function, with signs of dysregulated neuromuscular interactions and lower exercise tolerance; whether the nervous system causes these changes should be investigated.
triangulacion: The three sources are fully consistent; the conclusions reproduce the abstract and add the line of future research on the nervous system. The keywords reflect the physiological focus well.

tema: Systematic review of whether cytokine levels differ between patients with CFS/ME/SEID and healthy controls.
diseno: Systematic review in PubMed, Scopus, Medline and EMBASE; 16,702 records, 15 case-control studies included; quality assessment with STROBE.
hallazgos: Ten studies measured serum cytokines and four in other fluids; quality was moderate and the data consistent, but with no definitive cytokine pattern.
conclusion: It is inconclusive that cytokines have a definitive role or serve as reliable biomarkers, except for some evidence of a concurrent inflammatory process; standardized protocols and homogeneous populations are recommended.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the conclusions qualify the abstract by acknowledging some inflammatory process and adding methodological recommendations on case definitions and stratification.

tema: To assess whether there is evidence that metabolomic alterations contribute to the pathogenesis of ME/CFS/SEID.
diseno: Systematic review (PubMed, Scopus, Medline, EMBASE; 1994-2020); 11 observational case-control studies with metabolites in blood and urine; Joanna Briggs checklist.
hallazgos: Metabolites of the amino acid pathway were the most altered (7 of 10 blood studies), but no metabolite was consistently altered; urinary results were inconsistent.
conclusion: Methodological inconsistency provides little evidence that metabolomics contributes to pathogenesis; homogeneous criteria and methods are needed.
triangulacion: Consistent; the PDF conclusions are blunter in stating that, with current data, metabolomics does not contribute to pathogenesis.

tema: To compile and appraise the literature on mitochondrial alterations in ME/CFS/SEID compared with healthy controls.
diseno: Systematic review (Embase, PubMed, Scopus, Medline; 1995-2020); 19 studies; quality with the Joanna Briggs case-control checklist.
hallazgos: The studies addressed mitochondrial structure, DNA/RNA, respiratory function, metabolites and coenzymes, with inconsistent results.
conclusion: It is difficult to establish the mitochondrial role; genomics suggests it is not a primary mitochondrial disorder, although there could be secondary mitochondrial decline.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions add the nuance of not being a primary mitochondrial disorder and caution because of small samples.

tema: Systematic review of the phenotype, receptors, cytokine production and cytotoxicity of NK cells in ME/CFS.
diseno: Systematic review (Medline, Scopus, EMBASE, PubMed; 1994-2018) with Downs and Black and JBI quality assessment; 17 observational case-control studies.
hallazgos: Eleven studies assessed cytotoxicity, 14 phenotype and receptors, 3 cytokines, 6 lytic proteins and 4 degranulation; reduced NK cytotoxicity was the most consistent finding, with alterations in lytic proteins.
conclusion: Altered NK cytotoxicity is a reliable cellular model for investigating ME/CFS and could characterize a subgroup of patients.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree fully on NK cytotoxicity as the central finding; the conclusions add perforin as a secondary marker.

tema: Systematic review of structural and functional neurological changes in ME/CFS measured with neuroimaging and their relationship to onset, symptoms and severity.
diseno: Search in PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE and Web of Science (1994-2019); 55 studies in adults with ME/CFS versus healthy controls (MRI, PET, EEG); quality assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist.
hallazgos: Changes are described in grey and white matter volumes, cerebral blood flow, structure, sleep, EEG activity, functional connectivity and cognitive function, with widespread disruption of the autonomic nervous system network.
conclusion: Patients show morphological changes, white matter abnormalities and functional connectivity abnormalities, but the findings are not consistent across studies and their origin is unknown; more research is required.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and share caution about the inconsistency of the results; the keywords highlight grey matter volume and cerebral flow, while the abstract and conclusions emphasize autonomic dysfunction.

tema: To assess the efficacy of mitochondria-targeted nutraceuticals in ME/CFS.
diseno: Systematic review (PubMed, Embase, Medline, Web of Science; 1995-2020); 9 intervention studies; quality with the Rosendal scale.
hallazgos: Improvement in fatigue was observed in 6 of 9 studies; biochemical, psychological and quality-of-life parameters were also assessed.
conclusion: There is insufficient evidence on the efficacy of these nutraceuticals; well-designed studies are required.
triangulacion: Consistent; the conclusions detail the limitations (few studies, heterogeneous fatigue tools, small samples, short duration), more cautious than the 6/9 figure in the abstract.

tema: Systematic review of resting-state quantitative EEG (qEEG) in fibromyalgia, ME/CFS and long COVID to understand the neurophysiopathology of the latter.
diseno: Search in MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Web of Science (1994-2023); of 2510 records, 17 studies against healthy controls were included; quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa scale (moderate to high).
hallazgos: In fibromyalgia, lower slow-band activity (delta, theta, alpha) and higher beta activity predominated, a pattern different from that of ME/CFS. The few long COVID studies focused on cognition and showed mixed results.
conclusion: The qEEG patterns of fibromyalgia and ME/CFS follow opposite trends; more research is needed to identify long COVID phenotypes with similar EEG signatures, with a view to biomarkers and neuromodulation.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent in the focus on qEEG and delta/theta bands; the conclusions (preprint, with licence text) reaffirm the opposition of patterns and are cautious regarding long COVID.

tema: Systematic review of the association between genetic polymorphisms (SNPs) and fatigue in ME/CFS, cancer-related fatigue and fatigue in other diseases.
diseno: Systematic search in PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO and Sociological Abstracts; 50 articles included, grouped into ME/CFS, cancer-associated fatigue and fatigue in other diseases.
hallazgos: SNPs in immune regulatory and neurotransmitter pathways stood out in all three subgroups, with associations of TNFα, IL1b, IL4 and IL6. ME/CFS shared HLA, IFN-γ, 5-HT and NR3C1 polymorphisms with fatigue in other diseases.
conclusion: Cytokine SNPs would play a main role in the three fatigue subgroups; the authors propose using them to identify risk genes, patient subgroups and therapeutic targets.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the weight of immune and cytokine SNPs. The conclusions add the HPA axis and an orientation toward cancer fatigue and behavioural interventions, a focus less centred on ME/CFS. Part of the abstract contains manuscript metadata.

tema: Systematic review of cognitive profiles in fibromyalgia, CFS and functional neurological disorders to characterize functional cognitive disorder (FCD) and propose a unifying theory.
diseno: Systematic review of studies with cognitive outcomes: 52 in fibromyalgia, 95 in CFS and 39 in functional neurological disorder.
hallazgos: There is a discordance between frequent subjective cognitive symptoms and inconsistent objective deficits; deficits in selective and divided attention, slow processing and vulnerability to distraction were observed. Only a minority showed low effort on validity tests, and in CFS there was greater perceived effort.
conclusion: These conditions share attention-centred cognitive symptoms and could be placed on an FCD spectrum; the authors hypothesize that pain, fatigue and interoceptive monitoring reduce external attention, although they call for more research because of methodological heterogeneity.
triangulacion: The three sources converge on attentional dysfunction; the conclusions are more cautious than the abstract's discussion regarding the functional spectrum and add implications for clinical trials.

tema: Investigates the relationship between TGF-β, its receptors and fatigue severity in CFS.
diseno: Case-control study (conference abstract): 117 CFS patients and 40 controls; active and total TGF-β by luciferase bioassay, TGFBR1/2 expression by qPCR and fatigue by FIS; linear and ordinal regression.
hallazgos: There were no differences in serum TGF-β or TGFBR1/2 between CFS and controls; active TGF-β and the active/total ratio were higher in the severe fatigue group than in the mild one (p=0.04; p=0.02).
conclusion: Active/total TGF-β increases in patients with more severe fatigue, a finding that must be confirmed in a larger cohort.
triangulacion: The text labelled as the abstract belongs to another abstract in the conference book (methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis), so it is not valid; keywords and conclusions are consistent with the TGF-β study.

tema: Explores autonomic and inflammatory mechanisms of pain and fatigue in a combined population of fibromyalgia and ME/CFS.
diseno: Experimental medicine study (conference abstract) with patients and controls, baseline inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), autonomic challenge, hypermobility criteria and mediation analysis; sample size not stated.
hallazgos: ESR and CRP were higher in patients and correlated with fatigue and pain; the autonomic challenge amplified pain and fatigue more than in controls; ESR mediated the increase in fatigue and connective tissue traits mediated the increase in pain.
conclusion: First study of its kind according to the authors; it reinforces the baseline inflammatory abnormalities and their possible predictive and mechanistic role in autonomically induced pain and fatigue.
triangulacion: Keywords (autonomic dysfunction, joint hypermobility) and conclusions agree; the abstract is noisy text from another abstract (coeliac disease) and is not usable. The conclusions come from the discussion and include the results.

tema: Investigates catecholamine-dependent thermoregulatory responses in adolescents with CFS and their relationship to clinical symptoms.
diseno: Case-control study with 15 adolescents with CFS (12-18 years) and 57 healthy controls; plasma catecholamines and metanephrines before and after intense cooling of one hand; acral skin blood flow, tympanic temperature, heart rate and blood pressure during moderate cooling.
hallazgos: Patients reported more chills, sweating, skin colour changes and sensations of heat. At rest they had higher noradrenaline, adrenaline, heart rate and tympanic temperature; during cooling acral flow fell less, vasoconstriction occurred at a lower temperature and tympanic temperature dropped more.
conclusion: Adolescents with CFS show abnormal catecholaminergic thermoregulatory responses at rest and with local cooling, which supports the sympathetic dysfunction hypothesis and could explain clinical symptoms.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and reinforce one another around sympathetic dysfunction; the PDF conclusions are somewhat more cautious ('appear to support', 'could explain').

tema: To compare AMPK activation and glucose uptake in cultured muscle cells from CFS patients after electrical stimulation.
diseno: In vitro study with skeletal muscle cultures from 10 CFS patients and 7 controls, subjected to electrical pulse stimulation (EPS) for up to 24 h.
hallazgos: CFS cells showed higher baseline myogenin expression, no increase in AMPK phosphorylation or glucose uptake after 16 h of EPS (with preserved insulin response) and lower IL6 secretion.
conclusion: The persistence of these differences in culture points to a genetic/epigenetic mechanism and offers a system for identifying therapeutic targets.
triangulacion: Full coherence; the conclusions section reproduces the abstract (followed by introduction text, noise). Keywords aligned.

tema: Evaluates intranasal mechanical stimulation targeting the neuroimmune interface and its immunological correlate in ME.
diseno: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of intranasal mechanical stimulation (probably of the trigeminal nerve) for 8 weeks, with longitudinal monitoring of immune system components in blood and transcriptional analysis. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: A reduction of ~30% in the overall symptom score was observed; signs of chronic immune activation were detected, along with correlates of improvement centred on gut-homing immune cells and lower inflammation, with an increase in disease tolerance mechanisms.
conclusion: The authors suggest that ME could be explained by a maladaptive disease tolerance response after an infection; the mechanisms of the relief remain to be determined.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (vagus nerve, trigeminal, brainstem, PEM); the extracted conclusions are only contributions, funding and conflicts of interest, so they provide no conclusions.

tema: Evaluates proteins of the activin family as serum biomarkers for the diagnosis of CFS/ME.
diseno: Observational cross-sectional study in primary care: patients meeting the 2003 Canadian Criteria and healthy controls (18-65 years; female-to-male ratio >3:1); serum activin A, activin B, follistatin and cytokines, also compared with reference ranges. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Activin B was significantly elevated compared with controls and the reference range, with normal activin A and follistatin; routine pathology and cytokines (IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10, IL-17A, TNF, IFN-γ) did not differ.
conclusion: The combination of elevated activin B and normal activin A identifies CFS/ME patients and constitutes a possible serum test, which requires a larger prospective study.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent on activin B as a biomarker; the conclusions are somewhat more cautious in calling for a prospective study to assess its predictive ability.

tema: Analyses whether activity patterns in CFS (activity limitation and all-or-nothing behaviours) follow symptom experience and affect.
diseno: Study using experience sampling methodology (ESM) in 23 adults from UK CFS services; 10 daily assessments over 6 days via a mobile app; multilevel models.
hallazgos: Current fatigue and pain predicted greater activity limitation; subjective wellbeing predicted more all-or-nothing behaviours; contrary to the hypothesis, positive affect predicted limitation and negative affect predicted all-or-nothing.
conclusion: Symptoms appear to drive activity management patterns, in line with the cognitive-behavioural model of CFS; ESM with mHealth is feasible for studying these relationships.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and centred on the cognitive-behavioural model; the conclusions are more cautious than the abstract in acknowledging the small sample and tentative interpretation.

tema: Tests the hypothesis of CRFR2 receptor overexpression in ME/CFS and the efficacy of an acute dose of the agonist CT38s.
diseno: Open-label trial in 14 patients; subcutaneous infusion of CT38s at four dose levels (0.01-0.20 μg/kg/h) for a maximum of 10.5 h; primary outcome: change in the 28-day total daily symptom score (TDSS). Registration NCT03613129.
hallazgos: Patients were more sensitive to the haemodynamic effects of CRFR2 stimulation than healthy subjects from a previous trial; adverse effects were mild; TDSS improved in a sustained way, with −25.7% (p = 0.009) at 0.03 μg/kg/h, correlated with exposure and baseline severity.
conclusion: The results support the involvement of CRFR2 and acute CRFR2 agonism as a therapeutic approach worthy of further study.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent (receptor endocytosis, raphe nuclei, limbic system); the conclusions stress the pharmacokinetic dependence as an argument against a chance effect, without a placebo group.

tema: Links acute enterovirus infections to viral persistence and the subsequent development of ME/CFS.
diseno: Case series with longitudinal follow-up: hospitalized patients with acute fever screened for enterovirus; those who developed ME/CFS underwent endoscopy and antral biopsy with immunoperoxidase and viral RNA assay; 3 representative cases are presented.
hallazgos: Three patients with different manifestations of acute enterovirus infection progressed to chronic ME/CFS symptoms, with persistent viral infection demonstrated in the antrum years later.
conclusion: After acute infection, enteroviruses can persist and give rise to ME/CFS, possibly through a balance between attenuated intracellular viruses and an ineffective immune response.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the structured abstract and agree with it; the keywords (gastric biopsy, immunoperoxidase, viral persistence) faithfully reflect the methods and focus.

tema: Develops a diagnostic test for ME/CFS based on single-cell Raman spectroscopy of PBMC and artificial intelligence.
diseno: Diagnostic study with 98 subjects: 61 ME/CFS patients of varying severity and 37 healthy controls and controls with other diseases; Raman profiles of blood cells analysed with AI.
hallazgos: Raman profiles distinguished healthy individuals, controls with other diseases and patients with an accuracy of 91%, and differentiated mild, moderate and severe ME/CFS with 84%. Raman peaks that correlate with the phenotypes were identified.
conclusion: The method is promising for supporting the diagnosis and management of ME/CFS and could be extended to long COVID and post-Lyme syndrome.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (Raman, AI, severity classification, long COVID). No conclusions text is available, so it cannot be checked whether the authors qualify the scope.

tema: Viewpoint summarizing findings from a 2019 NIH conference on neuroendocrine, metabolic, immunological and physiological abnormalities in ME/CFS.
diseno: Opinion article/narrative review based on a conference; no own population.
hallazgos: Many biological measurements distinguish patients from healthy controls, but none yet has the sensitivity and specificity of a good diagnostic test; a small study (20 cases and 20 controls) showed perfect sensitivity without proven specificity against other fatiguing diseases.
conclusion: There are still no FDA-approved treatments or validated diagnostic tests, but growing interest and funding will allow progress toward effective therapies.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions provide specific nuances (lack of treatments and of a diagnostic test) that the brief abstract does not detail.
